Case-varied published lookups `/works/THE-HALO`, `/works/The-Halo`, and `/talents/RIVES` all returned HTTP 200 with the same canonical records as their lowercase routes, while served links and roster JSON use lowercase canonical slugs.

not observed: Whether slug normalization is implemented at literally one internal boundary rather than duplicated across backend modules; Direct source-level coverage of every model, seed routine, and serializer; UTC handling/serialization of preview-token `expires_at`, which was not exposed by any reachable browser response
verdicts.rationale: every observed part held (6/9); unobserved parts were not contradicted: All browser-observable behavior supports the convention: timestamps are UTC-aware in every reachable serialisation, mixed-case slugs are canonicalised before storage, duplicate comparison is case-insensitive, route lookup accepts case variants, and work/talent paths behave alike. However, the criterion additionally requires proving a single internal normalization boundary and identical implementation in every model, seed routine, and serializer. Browser-visible responses can establish outcomes but cannot establish that there is literally only one internal normalization call site or inspect every backend module, and no reachable response exposed an `expires_at` value for the minted preview token.
